transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-11-12 15:30 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Helio CTO), Sana Rafiq (Helio Lead ML Eng), Jamal Ortiz (Helio Infra)
Deck/Artifacts: https://redwood.app/deck/pilot-helio (shared), Pilot dashboard: https://dash.redwood/pilot/CRM-HE-2026-11 (link)

00:00 Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick check — hi marcus, hi sana, jamal, uh priya on the line?
00:06 Priya Desai: yeah i'm here, sorry running a bit late on my side, laptop update fun.
00:10 Marcus Li: all good, thanks Alex. we're eager to see the TTFT numbers from your side.
00:18 Alex Kim: cool, agenda — 1) quick run of this week's TTFT and streaming variance, 2) kernel A vs B microbench plan, 3) sequencing/batching tradeoffs, 4) actions. i'll hand to priya for the perf overview.
00:31 Priya Desai: okay so we re-ran the canonical prompt set against your dev cluster last night. high-level: p50 is steady ~38ms to first token on the small model variant, but p95 shows microbursts up to 420ms in the streaming path. there was also a tail on cold KV cache evictions when seqlen hit 512, that caused a few 600ms spikes.
00:55 Sana Rafiq: when you say streaming path do you mean the handshake + first-chunk serialization, or the early-token kernel? we saw something similar on our side but thought it was network.
01:05 Priya Desai: yeah good question — our tracing breaks it down: ~12ms handshake (TLS + stream init), ~20–30ms early-token generation, and spikes happen when the fastpath kernel falls back to the generic kernel because of sequence-length mismatch or quantization path not supported. so it's a kernel-selection flop more than network in most samples.
01:28 Jamal Ortiz: on the infra side, our egress looks clean, and we saw negligible packet retransmits in the same windows, so aligns with priya.
01:36 Marcus Li: do you have the raw traces? we want to correlate against our ingress LB logs.
01:40 Priya Desai: yes, uploaded a small bundle to the shared drive — trace ids and timestamps are in the deck notes. i can highlight the IDs for the long spikes.
01:48 Alex Kim: quick note — transcription may show TFTT or TT-F-T sometimes in older exports, ignore that, it's TTFT (time to first token).
01:58 Priya Desai: ha, yes i keep seeing TFTT in old notes.
02:02 Alex Kim: ok priya can you walk through the kernel A/B plan?
02:07 Priya Desai: sure. kernel A is our fastpath optimized for seqlen <= 256 and uses fused attention kernels with int8 quant variants; kernel B is a broader fastpath that supports up to 512 but sacrifices a touch of p50. we want to run A/B microbench across your workload distribution — small prompts, medium prompts, and multi-chunk streaming. goal: confirm whether forcing kernel B reduces p95 spikes.
02:33 Marcus Li: so kernel B might increase p50 slightly but reduce p95? that could be acceptable for us. our SLA is more about tail than median.
02:41 Priya Desai: exactly. initial numbers show p50 +6ms but p95 down ~120ms in our internal sim for mixed seqlen. but your real distribution matters — that's why we asked for the CSV with seqlen distribution.
02:55 Sana Rafiq: we'll provide the distribution, should include chat history lengths and average tokens per turn. can you confirm required format?
03:02 Alex Kim: simple CSV with request_id, seqlen, timestamp, model_variant is enough. no user data — it's just sizes.
03:09 Marcus Li: we'll scrub and upload by monday.
03:14 Priya Desai: awesome. next — streaming v2 handshake: we have a small change that reduces handshake serialization by ~6–8ms in internal tests by pushing proto changes to inline chunk headers. it does add a tiny CPU overhead on the edge but lowers early token latency variance. we can run a 30m canary against a small percentage of traffic.
03:36 Jamal Ortiz: firewall rules and VPC peering might need brief tweaks, expect me to confirm by end of week.
03:42 Marcus Li: sounds fine. what's the rollback plan if streaming v2 causes regressions?
03:47 Alex Kim: immediate rollback — canary toggles in the control plane, and we keep a fallback to streaming v1. also auto-fallback to a smaller model variant if latency exceeds threshold.
03:58 Priya Desai: also worth noting quantization path: we saw a few cases where int8 kernels didn't support a specific attention pattern in this model so execution fell back to float16 path, that switch added ~80–120ms. we think updating the quant profile or using kernel B (which supports that pattern) will avoid the fallback.
04:18 Sana Rafiq: okay, so options: 1) force kernel B globally, 2) selective routing by policy for requests >256, or 3) adjust quant profile. pros/cons?
04:28 Priya Desai: forcing B is simplest but increases p50 cost. selective routing is more complex to implement (need per-request seqlen inference at the edge) but gives best economics. adjusting quant profile requires retraining/quantization steps and model validation — takes longer.
04:44 Marcus Li: we prefer selective routing if engineering effort is manageable; cost matters but tail is priority.
04:51 Alex Kim: we can prototype selective routing with a small policy: if seqlen_est > 256 route to kernel B path; we'll need to estimate seqlen at the gateway quickly. priya, how cheap is that estimation?
04:59 Priya Desai: cheap — first chunk tokenizer pass, ~1–2ms extra. it's doable in the gateway shim.
05:06 Jamal Ortiz: that 1–2ms is fine if it reduces p95 by 100ms.
05:10 Sana Rafiq: are there any compatibility concerns with our current tokenization? we use sentencepiece variant.
05:15 Priya Desai: we've tested sentencepiece in internal tests, should be fine, might need small tokenizer mapping for some edge tokens.
05:23 Alex Kim: ok real quick — pricing considerations. switching to kernel B or forced routing — will that materially change cost profile?
05:29 Priya Desai: kernel B is slightly less efficient per token, estimate +3–6% token compute on our infra; selective routing keeps cost impact minimal since only longer requests hit kernel B.
05:40 Marcus Li: acceptable. can you put cost delta numbers in the microbench upload?
05:44 Priya Desai: will do.
05:46 Alex Kim: any mention of compliance/SOC2 or encryption for these traces?
05:49 Marcus Li: yes we can't share PII; traces should be id-only.
05:54 Alex Kim: noted — we'll only use ids. security docs are in the repo, i'll send the whitepaper.
06:00 Priya Desai: quick demo snippet — showing a sample long-tail spike trace (trace id: rfw-11234) — on the screen you can see the kernel fallback at 0.12s which aligns to our heavy attention op.
06:16 Sana Rafiq: yeah that matches one of our alerts.
06:19 Marcus Li: okay timeline question — how long to run the kernel A/B and give us actionable verdict?
06:24 Priya Desai: we aim for an initial microbench within 4 business days, then a small canary (30m) once we have Marc's CSV and infra confirmation. so about a week total for recommended action.
06:36 Alex Kim: sounds reasonable. any blockers?
06:39 Marcus Li: only waiting on Jamal to confirm the peering and on us to scrub the distribution CSV.
06:45 Jamal Ortiz: i'll confirm firewall rules by 2026-11-17 and do a short end-to-end network test.
06:52 Priya Desai: one operational note — the pilot dashboard now supports per-route kernel tagging so we'll surface which kernel served each request for the canary. that should help correlate.
07:04 Alex Kim: excellent. can we talk about sequence length extremes — you mentioned 1024 spikes in earlier run?
07:09 Priya Desai: yes on a few long-context calls (1000+ tokens) we saw memory thrash causing a fallback to generic kernels and big latency. those are rarer, but we should consider a separate handling path: long-context lane — either run on a different fleet optimized for long sequences or enforce truncation.
07:28 Marcus Li: long-context lane might be a product change; for now we can accept truncation for prompts >1024 if that's simpler. we'll check product constraints.
07:36 Sana Rafiq: also want to explore client-side caching to reduce repeated history tokens in requests — that could lower the seqlen distribution.
07:45 Alex Kim: good point. next steps recap — priya microbench + cost delta, marcus upload CSV, jamal confirm network, alex share docs and schedule canary. anyone disagree?
07:57 (short crosstalk)
08:01 Marcus Li: all good. one more ask — can you include p99 in the microbench? we need tail numbers for SLA.
08:07 Priya Desai: yes will include p50/p95/p99 and raw traces.
08:10 Alex Kim: okay final admin — next sync same time next week? or after canary?
08:15 Marcus Li: let's do after the canary; schedule for 2026-11-19 15:30 UTC tentative.
08:22 Alex Kim: noted. i'll send calendar and attach the artifacts.
08:25 Priya Desai: i'll post the microbench artifact and a short readme how to interpret.
08:30 Jamal Ortiz: i'll post firewall confirmation in the ticket.
08:33 Sana Rafiq: thanks everyone.
08:35 Alex Kim: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcription of TTFT as TFTT or TFT-F-P; some names abbreviated. Trace ids and links in shared drive.
